import datetime

def count_melbourne_posts(start_date, end_date):
    # Assuming the data is fetched and stored in a list of post dates
    posts = ["2024-01-01", "2024-01-03", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-08", "2024-01-10", "2024-01-12", "2024-01-15", "2024-01-17", "2024-01-19", "2024-01-22", "2024-01-24", "2024-01-26", "2024-01-29", "2024-01-31"]

    # Initialize a dictionary to store the count of posts for each week
    weekly_counts = {}

    # Define the start date and the end date
    start_date = datetime.datetime.strptime(start_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
    end_date = datetime.datetime.strptime(end_date, "%Y-%m-%d")

    # Loop through each week
    while start_date <= end_date:
        # Calculate the end date of the week
        week_end_date = start_date + datetime.timedelta(days=6)

        # Format the start and end dates of the week
        week_start_date_str = start_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        week_end_date_str = week_end_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")

        # Count the number of posts in the current week
        weekly_post_count = sum(1 for post_date in posts if start_date <= datetime.datetime.strptime(post_date, "%Y-%m-%d") <= week_end_date)

        # Store the count of posts for the current week
        weekly_counts[week_start_date_str] = weekly_post_count

        # Move to the next week
        start_date += datetime.timedelta(days=7)

    return weekly_counts
